channel.title: National Public Radio (NPR) - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from National Public Radio (NPR) (npr.org)

item.title: U.K. arrests ex-ambassador to the U.S. on suspicion of misconduct over Epstein ties
item.description: Police have arrested Peter Mandelson, a veteran Labour Party politician who served as British ambassador to the U.S., as part of an investigation into his ties with Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Huge snowstorm in the Northeast forces millions to stay home
item.description: Meteorologists said the storm is the strongest in a decade, dumping more than 2 feet of snow across the Northeast.

item.title: Kate Hudson on regret, rom-coms and finding a role that hits all the notes
item.description: Hudson always wanted to sing, but feared it would derail her acting career. Now she's up for an Oscar for her portrayal of a hairdresser who performs in a Neil Diamond tribute band in Song Sung Blue.

item.title: A new lawsuit alleges DHS illegally tracked and intimidated observers
item.description: Observers watching federal immigration enforcement in Maine who were told by agents they were "domestic terrorists" and would be added to a "database" or "watchlist" are now part of a new federal class action lawsuit.

item.title: 'Everything was in pieces:' Lindsey Vonn describes grueling surgery on broken leg
item.description: In a recent video, the Olympic skier credits her surgeon with saving her leg from potential amputation.

item.title: BAFTAs apologize after guest with Tourette syndrome uses racial slur during ceremony
item.description: A man with Tourette syndrome shouted a racial slur and other offensive remarks during the BAFTA awards ceremony Sunday. The BBC did not edit out his outbursts in its delayed broadcast.

item.title: The FDA creates a quicker path for gene therapies
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration aims to evaluate treatments for rare diseases based on plausible evidence that they would work — without requiring a clinical trial first.

item.title: In pictures: Winter storm slams the east coast
item.description: Photos of cities in Connecticut, New York, New Jersey and Massachusetts as they cope with a powerful winter storm.

item.title: GOP Rep. Tony Gonzales faces pressure from party over affair allegations
item.description: The Texas Republican is facing calls from fellow House Republicans to resign, following allegations of an affair with a staffer who later died by suicide.

item.title: France moves to bar US Ambassador Charles Kushner from direct government access
item.description: France's top diplomat has requested that U.S. Ambassador Charles Kushner no longer be allowed direct access to members of the French government. Kushner skipped a meeting Monday to discuss comments by the Trump administration over the beating death of a far-right activist.
